chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad narrated from Ubayd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Nahyakī, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from a number of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Abd Allah al-Qasari, who said:

I was in al-Madina when a boy who had stolen was brought to me. I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Ask him where he stole; did he know that there was a punishment for theft?' If he said 'Yes,' I said, 'What is that punishment?' If he did not know that the punishment for theft was cutting (the hand), then let him go free.' He said: 'So I took the boy and asked him, and I said to him, 'Did you know that there is a punishment for theft?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'What is it?' He said, 'I am struck (with the cane).' So I let him go free.'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a child to be subject to the hand-cutting punishment for theft in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *al-Istibsar* clarifies the condition of *'ilm* (knowledge) as a prerequisite for the fixed punishment of *qat' al-yad* in minors, distinguishing between general awareness of theft's wrongfulness and specific knowledge of the legal penalty. Imam al-Sadiq (a) demonstrates a nuanced judicial approach by verifying the boy's cognitive grasp of the specific consequence; since the boy only knew he would be struck, he was exempt from the more severe amputation. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the hadd punishment requires both the act and the conscious understanding of its specific legal status.
